extracted.intended_audience: Investors in Vanguard mutual funds and ETFs; individual shareholders considering proxy participation
extracted.subtask_description: Describes Vanguard's approaches, policies, and investor participation options for proxy voting across its funds, including the Investor Choice program for eligible individual investors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range of approaches to proxy voting
rubrics_metrics.description: A range of approaches to proxy voting, with a focus on long-term investment returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vanguard offers more than 400 funds that are managed by over two dozen investment managers, each with their own policies and approaches to proxy voting. This implies variability in how votes are evaluated and cast across different funds and managers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investor Choice participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Vanguard's Investor Choice program enables individual investors in certain equity index funds to express their perspectives on shareholder matters at the companies held in their funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investor Choice provides investors in certain Vanguard-advised mutual funds and ETFs the opportunity to participate more directly in the proxy voting process. Availability is limited to eligible funds (certain equity index funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: How proxy voting works (information & choices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn about what proxy voting is, the ways in which Vanguard funds approach proxy voting, and how investors can participate in Vanguard’s Investor Choice program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page positions itself as an informational resource covering the mechanics of proxy voting, fund-level approaches, and participation options. Investors should consult these materials to understand choices available to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Votes administered in accordance with stated voting policies and fund objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers administer proxy voting in accordance with the stated voting policies and in pursuit of each fund’s stated investment objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proxy votes are to be cast consistent with each fund's documented voting policy and with an eye toward fulfilling that fund's investment objective—indicating alignment between voting decisions and fund strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal and external manager voting responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Across Vanguard’s more than 400 funds worldwide, some two dozen internal and external investment managers cast proxy votes on behalf of the respective funds—or portion of funds—that they manage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both internal and external managers may have voting authority; the identity and type of manager can affect the applicable voting policy and approach for a given fund or portion of a fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on long-term investment returns
rubrics_metrics.description: Proxy voting approaches emphasize a focus on long-term investment returns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The stated objective of Vanguard's proxy voting approaches is to support long-term returns, suggesting that proposals and voting decisions are evaluated through that lens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard investor disclosures / risk notice
rubrics_metrics.description: All investing is subject to risk, including the possible loss of principal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proxy voting and any investment decision remain subject to general investment risks; Vanguard includes standard disclosures to remind investors of these risks.
